newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes restoration of Serbia opposition win.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes restoration of Serbia opposition win.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday welcomed a vote by Serbia's parliament reinstating opposition victories in local elections but warned against any attempt by the ruling Socialists to take away powers from local councils.
"We welcome the actions by the Serbian parliament yesterday evening ... as an important move in the right direction," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

After a stand-off of nearly three months, the parliament on Tuesday passed a law reinstating victories by the Zajedno opposition coalition in 14 cities, including Belgrade, annulled for "irregularities" after elections on Nov. 17.
Burns told reporters that Washington was urging "rapid and fair implementation" of the law, and that municipal assets, including local broadcast media, be transferred to the opposition.

"If there's any attempt made by the Serbian government to strip away the assets of power, the ability to print, the ability to broadcast, the ability to control civil services ... that would be of great concern," Burns said.
"We will wait to see the concrete deeds of the Serbian government in allowing these politicians to have effective control of the instruments of government," he said.
He also called on the government of President Slobodan Milosevic to open a formal dialogue with the opposition to start a process of democratization.
Burns said a trip to Belgrade by Assistant Secretary of State for Human Rights John Shattuck was under consideration although no final decision had been made.
Officials of Shattuck's seniority have stayed away from Serbia since the elections crisis erupted, but Burns denied there had been a formal ban on such visits.
Turning to Bosnia, Burns said the United States condemned expulsions of Moslems by Croats in Croat-controlled areas of the divided city of Mostar.

"We call upon the Croat authorities to allow the ... Moslems to return to their homes at once," he said. "Such actions violate both the letter and the spirit of the Dayton accords (on Bosnia) ... and therefore they are of great concern to the United States."
